Living in Bridgeland, Calgary

If you've been searching for Bridgeland Calgary homes, you've already discovered one of the city's best-kept secrets — though it's not much of a secret anymore. Bridgeland is one of Calgary's most sought-after inner-city communities, blending historic charm with modern urban living just minutes from downtown. Once known as Calgary's "Little Italy," the neighbourhood has evolved into a vibrant, walkable enclave of tree-lined streets, indie cafes, river pathways, and a thriving real estate market that consistently attracts buyers from across the city. Whether you're a young professional craving a walkable lifestyle or a family looking for a tight-knit community with genuine character, Bridgeland delivers on all fronts. Raman Basra and the team at ramanbasra.ca have helped countless buyers find their perfect home in Bridgeland — and it's easy to see why this community keeps rising to the top of buyer wishlists.

Location & Getting Around

Bridgeland sits in Calgary's City Centre quadrant, tucked just northeast of downtown across the Bow River. The community is bounded by Memorial Drive NE to the south, Edmonton Trail NE to the west, and 8th Street NE to the east — giving residents exceptional access to the city core. Downtown Calgary is a 10-minute walk or a quick C-Train ride from the Bridgeland/Riverside Station on the Blue Line. Commuters benefit from fast access to Deerfoot Trail, Centre Street, and Memorial Drive. Cyclists and pedestrians are equally well-served, with the Bow River Pathway running along the southern edge of the community and connecting riders and walkers to both downtown and the wider pathway network. For errands and everyday needs, Bridgeland's Walk Score consistently ranks among the highest in Calgary.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

Bridgeland has a distinctive energy that's hard to replicate in newer suburban communities. The streets feel lived-in and authentic, with heritage character homes sitting comfortably beside sleek modern infills and boutique condo buildings. The community attracts young professionals, couples, and established families alike — all drawn by the same thing: a neighbourhood where people actually know their neighbours. The commercial strip along 1 Avenue NE is the community's beating heart, lined with independent restaurants, specialty coffee shops, boutiques, and lively gathering spots. Weekend mornings bring joggers and dog-walkers to Bridgeland Park, while summer evenings fill the patios of the neighbourhood's many acclaimed eateries. The Bridgeland Community Association runs regular events, fitness programs, and social gatherings that keep the community connected year-round. It's urban living done right — vibrant, but never overwhelming.

Schools & Education

Bridgeland is well-served by both CBE and CSSD schools. On the public side, Riverside School (CBE, K–9) is a popular science-based learning program located within the community itself. Colonel Macleod School (CBE, 4–9) is situated just northeast and offers both regular and traditional learning programs. High school students attend Crescent Heights High School (CBE, 10–12), a well-established institution known for its Advanced Placement courses, strong athletics program, and academic support. For Catholic education, St. Alphonsus School (CSSD, K–9) offers a dual-track program including an Italian language stream — a meaningful nod to Bridgeland's multicultural heritage. Catholic high schoolers attend Father Lacombe High School, which offers diverse programming and extracurriculars.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

Bridgeland Park sits at the centre of community life, featuring a soccer pitch, tennis courts, baseball diamond, community garden, children's playground, off-leash dog area, disc golf course, and a toboggan run for winter fun. The Bow River Pathway puts miles of paved cycling and walking routes at residents' doorsteps, connecting south toward Pearce Estate Park and west into downtown. Perhaps Bridgeland's most enviable amenity is its immediate proximity to the Calgary Zoo and the Telus Spark Science Centre — both world-class family destinations accessible by foot or bike. St. Patrick's Island, a beautifully restored river island park, is also a short walk away, offering stunning Calgary skyline views and peaceful green space that feels a world apart from the city.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Bridgeland's walkable commercial strip along 1 Avenue NE punches well above its weight for a neighbourhood of its size. Dining highlights include Shiki Menya for acclaimed Japanese ramen, UNA Pizza + Wine for wood-fired Neapolitan pies, OEB Breakfast Co. for elevated morning fare, and Blue Star Diner for locally sourced comfort food. The Bridgeland Market is a beloved local institution offering specialty groceries, fresh produce, and artisan products. The neighbourhood also has day spas, yoga studios, boutique fitness centres, and professional services all within easy walking distance. For larger shopping runs, Deerfoot City and North Hill Centre are a short drive north or east via Edmonton Trail.

Real Estate in Bridgeland

The Bridgeland real estate market offers one of Calgary's most diverse housing selections. The community includes heritage character homes from the early 1900s, modern infill detached houses, townhouses, and a robust selection of condominiums — making it accessible across a wide range of budgets and lifestyles.

As of mid-2026, the average active listing price in Bridgeland/Riverside sits between $571,000 and $730,000 depending on property type. Condominiums represent the most affordable entry point, with prices starting around $185,000 for smaller units and averaging approximately $396,000 — a strong value proposition for first-time buyers and investors, particularly given the neighbourhood's robust rental demand (roughly 53% of residents rent). Townhouses command higher prices, ranging from $469,900 to over $1,199,900 and averaging around $680,000, reflecting the premium buyers place on attached ground-level living in this highly walkable setting. Detached infill homes and heritage character properties represent the top of the market.

Market conditions in 2026 lean slightly toward buyers in the condo segment due to increased citywide supply, while detached homes and townhouses remain competitive. Bridgeland's inner-city location, limited land availability, and enduring lifestyle appeal make it a strong long-term hold for both investors and owner-occupiers. Days on market have been consistently among the lowest in Calgary, with well-priced homes regularly attracting multiple offers. If you're considering buying in Bridgeland, acting decisively is key.

Why Choose Bridgeland?

  • Unbeatable walkability: One of Calgary's highest Walk Scores — restaurants, shops, parks, and transit are all steps from your front door.
  • Inner-city location: Downtown Calgary is a 10-minute walk or a single C-Train stop away, making car-free commuting genuinely practical.
  • Diverse housing options: From entry-level condos under $250K to luxury infills over $1M, Bridgeland has something for every budget and lifestyle.
  • World-class amenities at your doorstep: The Calgary Zoo, Telus Spark, St. Patrick's Island, and the Bow River Pathway are all immediately accessible.
  • Authentic community character: A neighbourhood with real history, thriving local businesses, and a community association that keeps the social calendar full year-round.

Living in New Brighton

If you're searching for New Brighton Calgary homes, you've likely already heard the buzz about this charming southeast community. New Brighton is a master-planned neighbourhood that effortlessly blends English-inspired architecture, resort-style amenities, and a warm, family-oriented culture. Whether you're a first-time buyer, a growing family, or an investor looking for a community with proven staying power, New Brighton consistently ranks among Calgary's most desirable places to call home. As a trusted Calgary real estate professional, Raman Basra has helped countless buyers navigate the New Brighton market — and it's easy to see why this community keeps rising to the top of wish lists in 2026.

Location & Getting Around

New Brighton sits in the southeast quadrant of Calgary, bounded by 130th Avenue SE to the north, Stoney Trail to the east, and McKenzie Towne to the west. The community enjoys quick access to Deerfoot Trail and Stoney Trail, making commutes across the city manageable. Residents typically reach downtown Calgary in about 20 minutes by car. While the neighbourhood is primarily car-dependent, the 130th Avenue transit corridor provides bus service connecting residents to the broader Calgary Transit network, with MAX Yellow BRT service within a short drive.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

New Brighton stands out for its distinctive Old English architectural character — think carriage-style garage doors, arched entryways, and charming window boxes that give the streetscapes a cohesive, storybook feel. The community has no through-traffic cutting across it, which creates a safe, quiet atmosphere that families absolutely love. At the heart of the neighbourhood is the New Brighton Residents Association (NBRA), which runs a packed schedule of programming for all ages: chair yoga, learn-to-skate sessions, teen painting nights, summer barbecues, and holiday events. The 6,500-square-foot New Brighton Clubhouse serves as the social hub, and the sense of community pride here is palpable. Neighbours know each other, kids play freely in the parks, and the streets feel genuinely alive.

Schools & Education

New Brighton is well-served by both public and Catholic schools, making it a top choice for families with school-age children. On the public side, New Brighton School (CBE, K–5) is located right in the community at 30 New Brighton Drive SE and enrols approximately 580 students. Students then transition to Dr. Martha Cohen School (CBE, Grades 6–9) for junior high. Catholic families are served by St. Marguerite School (CSSD, K–6), which is also nearby. For high school, students typically attend Bishop McNally High School (CSSD) or Joane Cardinal-Schubert High School (CBE), both accessible via transit or a short drive.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

New Brighton's recreational infrastructure is one of its biggest selling points. The centrepiece is the Brighton Pond and Central Park, a sprawling 30-acre green space perfect for morning walks, picnics, and birdwatching. The New Brighton Athletic Park features four multi-use turf fields for soccer, lacrosse, ultimate frisbee, and field hockey, plus a baseball diamond and a popular skatepark. The Clubhouse grounds include two tennis courts, a pickleball court, a beach volleyball court, basketball courts, a splash park, and a winter hockey rink with a cozy fireplace area. Extensive paved pathways connect parks and green spaces throughout the community, making it easy to bike, jog, or stroll without ever touching a main road.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Daily errands are a breeze for New Brighton residents. New Brighton Square provides quick-stop retail right in the community. Just five minutes away, McKenzie Towne Centre — anchored by Sobeys and GoodLife Fitness — covers grocery, pharmacy (Rexall), banking (Scotiabank, ATB), and more. McKenzie Towne High Street offers a unique village-style shopping experience with boutique shops, cafés, pizza restaurants, and sushi spots. For major retail, Deerfoot Meadows is a short drive and includes IKEA, Best Buy, Banana Republic, and a wide range of restaurants. Fish Creek Provincial Park, one of Canada's largest urban parks, is only 15 minutes away for those who crave nature on demand.

Real Estate in New Brighton

The New Brighton Calgary real estate market is active and competitive in 2026. As of mid-2026, there are approximately 44 active listings, with an average asking price around $524,000–$549,000. The market breakdown by property type is as follows:

  • Detached single-family homes typically range from $450,000 to $750,000, with luxury options reaching $900,000. These homes showcase the neighbourhood's signature Old English architecture and generous lot sizes.
  • Townhouses average around $406,000, ranging from approximately $355,000 to $540,000 — an excellent entry point for first-time buyers and downsizers alike.
  • Condos and apartments start from around $200,000–$250,000, making New Brighton one of the more accessible SE communities for buyers on tighter budgets.

Market velocity is a standout story: approximately 100% of homes are selling within 10 days, with around 4.5% going above asking price — both figures above Calgary's citywide average. This strong absorption rate reflects sustained demand driven by the community's premium amenities, design character, and relative affordability compared to newer lake communities like Mahogany or Auburn Bay. For investors, New Brighton has demonstrated consistent long-term appreciation and strong rental demand given its family-friendly profile. Whether you're buying your first home or adding to a real estate portfolio, New Brighton offers compelling fundamentals in 2026.

Why Choose New Brighton?

  • Resort-style amenities included: The NBRA Clubhouse, Brighton Pond, tennis courts, splash park, and skating rink are exclusive to residents and create an unmatched community experience.
  • Distinctive Old English architecture: New Brighton's character homes set it apart visually from other SE communities, with a cohesive aesthetic that holds strong curb appeal and resale value.
  • Excellent schools close to home: With both CBE and CSSD options at elementary, junior high, and high school levels, families have strong choices without long commutes.
  • Fast-selling market with upside: Homes sell quickly and consistently, and prices remain more accessible than comparable lake communities — making it a smart buy in the current market.
  • Strong community culture: Active residents association, year-round programming, and a no-through-traffic layout create a genuinely close-knit neighbourhood where families thrive long-term.

Location & Getting Around

Carrington sits in the north-northwest quadrant of Calgary, positioned just north of Nolan Hill and east of the Rocky Ridge corridor. The community's location along Stoney Trail and Symons Valley Parkway makes it exceptionally well connected — you can reach downtown Calgary in roughly 25 minutes under normal traffic, and Calgary International Airport is a quick 15-minute drive east. Major commercial nodes like Beacon Hill, Sage Hill Crossing, and Creekside are all within a 10-minute drive. A future Centre Street BRT/LRT extension is planned to bring rapid transit closer to the community, making Carrington an increasingly smart long-term location for transit-minded buyers.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

Carrington was designed with the tagline "connection" front and centre — and it shows. The streetscapes are walkable, the homes front onto parks and pathways, and neighbours actually interact here. The community skews young: you'll find a lot of millennial families, dual-income couples, and new Canadians who appreciate the combination of affordability and modern construction. Trico Homes, Excel Homes, Truman, and other quality builders have developed varied housing types that keep the streetscape feeling fresh without being monotonous.

Community events organised through the Carrington Residents' Association bring people together throughout the year — summer block parties, holiday lights competitions, and weekend pop-up markets at Greenway Park give the neighbourhood an energy that newer communities sometimes lack. The vibe here is optimistic and forward-looking: people moved to Carrington because they saw its potential, and that shared excitement translates into a strong sense of pride in the area.

Schools & Education

Families with school-age children are well served in Carrington. On the public side, Kenneth D. Taylor School (Calgary Board of Education) serves students within the community. For Catholic families, the Calgary Catholic School District operates St. Josephine Bakhita School nearby. Our Lady of Grace School is another nearby option for families seeking faith-based education. The area is also within reasonable distance of several strong high schools in the broader NW quadrant. For parents of younger children, multiple licensed daycares and preschools have established themselves within and adjacent to the community as the population has grown.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

Carrington's outdoor credentials are one of its standout features. The community encompasses more than 65 acres of green space, including an environmental reserve, interconnected trail networks, and quiet stormwater ponds that attract local wildlife. Greenway Park is the neighbourhood's social hub — it features playgrounds, a basketball court, electrical outlets for community events, and direct access to the Rotary/Mattamy Greenway Trail System, a city-wide multi-use pathway that links Carrington to communities throughout northwest Calgary. A short drive south brings residents to Nose Hill Park, one of Calgary's largest urban natural areas, offering hiking, off-leash dog walking, and sweeping city views. Baseball diamonds and soccer fields are also part of the longer-term park plan as the community reaches buildout.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Day-to-day conveniences are easy to access in and around Carrington. Within the community, Carrington Green (developed by Royop) is the neighbourhood's retail hub, offering grocery shopping, professional services, and quick-service dining. For a broader retail experience, residents are a short drive from Beacon Hill Shopping Centre, Sage Hill Crossing, Evanston Towne Centre, and Gates of Nolan Hill — all of which offer major grocery chains, pharmacy, restaurants, fitness studios, and specialty retail. The Creekside Shopping Centre along Shaganappi Trail adds even more dining and service options. As the community continues to grow, additional commercial development within Carrington itself is planned.

Real Estate in Carrington

The Carrington Calgary real estate market in 2026 offers remarkable diversity across price points, making it accessible to a wide range of buyers. Single-family detached homes — the most popular housing type — typically range from the low $600s to just under $1 million for larger, upgraded models on premium lots. Townhomes and street towns are available from approximately $450,000 to $580,000, offering a practical entry point for buyers who want new construction without stretching their budget. Condo and apartment-style units start closer to $300,000, giving first-time buyers a genuine foothold in a growing community.

The overall average home price in Carrington sits around $574,000 as of mid-2026 — approximately 13% below the Calgary city average — which represents exceptional value given the quality of construction and neighbourhood amenities. The Calgary market overall has seen modest price softening in 2026, with the citywide benchmark around $569,000, down about 2% year-over-year. Detached homes have held their value best during this period, while townhomes offer more negotiating room for buyers.

Carrington is still in active development, which means buyers can choose between resale homes and brand-new builds from multiple builders — a flexibility that most established Calgary communities can't offer. Inventory levels are healthy, meaning buyers aren't facing the frantic bidding wars of 2022–2024, making this an excellent window to purchase with conditions and proper due diligence.

Why Choose Carrington?

  • Outstanding value: Average prices sit 13% below the Calgary benchmark, with modern homes and strong builder quality.
  • New construction choice: Multiple active builders mean buyers can customise finishes and floor plans not available in established neighbourhoods.
  • Excellent connectivity: Stoney Trail access makes commuting straightforward, and future transit expansion adds long-term upside.
  • Green space and lifestyle: 65+ acres of parks, the Rotary/Mattamy Greenway, and proximity to Nose Hill Park deliver an active outdoor lifestyle.
  • Strong community identity: Despite being a newer community, Carrington already has an engaged residents' association and a growing sense of place.

Living in Copperfield: Calgary's Best-Value SE Neighbourhood Guide (2026)

If you're searching for Copperfield Calgary homes that offer an unbeatable mix of affordability, lifestyle, and community spirit, you've landed in the right place. Copperfield is one of Southeast Calgary's most beloved master-planned communities — a neighbourhood where scenic ponds, winding pathways, and friendly streets come together to create something genuinely special. Whether you're a first-time buyer, a growing family, or an investor looking for a strong-performing asset, Copperfield delivers consistent value in one of the city's most desirable quadrants. Raman Basra and the team at ramanbasra.ca have helped countless buyers find their perfect home in Copperfield — and this guide breaks down everything you need to know before making your move.

Location & Getting Around

Copperfield sits in Calgary's southeast quadrant, tucked between 52nd Street SE and Stoney Trail — two of the city's most important arterials. This gives residents near-seamless access to the ring road and, by extension, every corner of the city. A commute to downtown Calgary takes roughly 25 minutes by car, while transit connections along 52nd Street SE link to the broader CTrain network. The neighbourhood is also well positioned relative to the nearby communities of Mahogany, Auburn Bay, and McKenzie Towne, putting a wealth of amenities within a short drive.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

Developed in the early 2000s by Hopewell Residential, Copperfield was always designed with livability front of mind. The result is a neighbourhood that feels cohesive and considered — tree-lined boulevards, eco-friendly pathways, picturesque ponds, and three distinct wetland areas give the community a resort-like atmosphere that residents genuinely appreciate. The Copperfield–Mahogany Community Association keeps the social calendar full with workshops, seasonal events, and community hall rentals that bring neighbours together year-round. In winter, the community skating rink becomes a neighbourhood gathering point. The demographics skew toward young families and dual-income couples, giving Copperfield an energetic, optimistic vibe that's hard to replicate in older, more established communities.

Schools & Education

Families with children will find strong public and Catholic schooling options within or adjacent to Copperfield. Copperfield School (Calgary Board of Education, K–5) is located right in the heart of the neighbourhood at 54 Copperstone Road SE, offering a personalized learning environment with a strong music program and a variety of extracurricular clubs. On the Catholic side, St. Isabella School (Calgary Catholic School District, K–9) serves approximately 920 students from Copperfield, Elgin, and Inverness — one of the larger Catholic schools in the southeast. Older students typically attend high schools in the wider SE catchment, and French immersion options are accessible via FrancoSud.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

Copperfield's outdoor infrastructure is a genuine standout. The community contains seven parks, four playgrounds, and three ponds and wetland areas all woven together by over 15 kilometres of paved walking and cycling trails. Copperfield Park is the neighbourhood's central green hub, featuring open sports fields, picnic areas, and playgrounds. Just beyond the community boundary, Ralph Klein Park offers wetland boardwalks and environmental education opportunities, while the New Brighton Athletic Park provides soccer fields, a skate park, and tennis courts for sports enthusiasts of all ages. The Community Hall adds an outdoor basketball court and a seasonal ice rink, rounding out one of the most complete recreational offerings in SE Calgary.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Day-to-day errands are easy in Copperfield thanks to proximity to two major retail nodes. South Trail Crossing, located just minutes away on 130th Avenue SE, is one of Calgary's largest power centres — home to major grocery chains, big-box retailers, pharmacies, banks, and dozens of dining options ranging from quick-service to sit-down restaurants. South Pointe adds additional retail and service options just a short drive south. The 130th Avenue corridor is a commercial hub rivalled by few parts of the city, meaning residents rarely need to travel far for anything. The nearby Seton Urban District also brings a hospital (South Health Campus), movie theatre, YMCA, and a growing restaurant scene within easy reach.

Real Estate in Copperfield

Copperfield's real estate market in 2026 is active and well-balanced, offering something at nearly every price point — a rarity in today's Calgary market. The neighbourhood average home price sits at approximately $468,000, with the current active listing pool (roughly 73 properties as of mid-2026) ranging from the low $200,000s for condominiums up to $849,000+ for larger detached homes.

Detached homes in Copperfield typically range between $500,000 and $750,000, with premium lots or fully renovated properties occasionally exceeding that threshold. These properties are selling in the 20–32 day range, reflecting healthy but not frenzied demand. Townhouses are priced between $339,000 and $525,000 (average around $416,000), making them an excellent option for first-time buyers or downsizers. Condominiums offer the most accessible entry point, with an average price near $290,000 — among the most affordable ownership options in southeast Calgary.

Unlike some of Calgary's newest communities where buyers pay a premium for unproven infrastructure, Copperfield offers a mature neighbourhood with established schools, parks, and transit, often at lower price points than comparable newer communities. Appreciation has been steady rather than speculative, which makes Copperfield a reliable long-term hold. The $364-per-square-foot average compares favourably to much of SE Calgary, and the breadth of property types means the neighbourhood attracts a diverse buyer pool — further supporting price resilience.

Why Choose Copperfield?

  • Outstanding value for money: Detached homes, townhouses, and condos at price points that remain accessible compared to many comparable SE communities.
  • Built-in lifestyle infrastructure: 15+ km of pathways, 7 parks, 3 scenic ponds, and a full suite of community recreation facilities — all within the neighbourhood itself.
  • Strong schools on your doorstep: Both CBE and CSSD schools within or immediately adjacent to the community, ideal for families with children of all ages.
  • Unmatched retail access: The 130th Avenue SE corridor, South Trail Crossing, South Pointe, and nearby Seton put everyday conveniences and premium amenities within minutes.
  • Mature community, proven track record: Two decades of community-building means established trees, finished amenities, and a strong neighbourhood identity — without the growing pains of newer developments.

Living in Chestermere

If you're searching for Chestermere Calgary homes that offer something truly special — a genuine lake at your doorstep, a tight-knit community feel, and surprising proximity to the city — Chestermere consistently tops the list for families, young professionals, and those looking to upsize from Calgary's core. Sitting just east of the city along the Trans-Canada Highway, Chestermere has evolved from a quiet lakeside retreat into one of the Calgary region's fastest-growing cities, and with good reason. Whether you're relocating from another province or simply looking for more space and lifestyle value, Raman Basra and the team at ramanbasra.ca are ready to help you find your perfect home in this thriving lakeside community.

Location & Getting Around

Chestermere is located approximately 20 kilometres east of downtown Calgary along Highway 1 (Trans-Canada Highway). The city sits just past the Calgary city limits in Rocky View County, making it an independent municipality with its own lower property tax rates. Most residents commute into Calgary via Stoney Trail (Highway 201) or directly along 17 Avenue SE, with the drive typically taking 20–30 minutes depending on traffic. Future plans from the Calgary Metropolitan Region Board include an extension of the 17 Avenue SE Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) corridor eastward through Chestermere Boulevard, which will further improve transit connectivity for residents who prefer not to drive.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

What makes Chestermere stand out from every other Calgary suburb is the lake. Chestermere Lake is the heart of the city — a year-round recreational hub where residents swim, kayak, paddleboard, and ice skate depending on the season. The waterfront lifestyle creates a relaxed, resort-town atmosphere that is rare this close to a major city. The community is known for its close-knit, welcoming character: neighbours tend to know each other, community events bring people together regularly, and the slower pace of life is a deliberate draw for families fleeing Calgary's denser neighbourhoods. Community festivals, seasonal markets, and lakeside gatherings are staples of the Chestermere social calendar throughout the year. The demographic skews toward young families and move-up buyers, with a growing population that now exceeds 25,000 residents — yet it still manages to feel far smaller and more personal than the number suggests.

Schools & Education

Chestermere is served by two school authorities. Rocky View Schools (RVS) is the public board operating in the area, with Chestermere High School serving grades 10–12 and drawing students from across the city. On the Catholic side, the Calgary Catholic School District (CSSD) operates several schools in Chestermere, including St. Gabriel School (K–12), Our Lady of Wisdom (K–6), and St. Gabriel Middle School (grades 6–9). An additional new Catholic K–9 school is planned to open at 800 West Lakeview Drive in Fall 2027, reflecting the growing demand from Chestermere's expanding family population. Rocky View Schools has also been actively building new capacity to keep pace with rapid enrolment growth across the region.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

Outdoor living is central to Chestermere's identity. Anniversary Park and John Peake Park are two of the most beloved green spaces, both offering direct lake access, picnic areas, and year-round recreation. Clearwater Park serves the newer southwest communities with open fields and pathway connections. The Chestermere Regional Community Association (CRCA), located on the northwest shore of Chestermere Lake, is the city's premier recreation hub — featuring baseball diamonds, soccer pitches, an indoor curling rink, and an artificial turf soccer pitch. The Chestermere Recreation Centre adds further indoor amenities including sport courts and event facilities. An extensive pathway network winds throughout the city, connecting neighbourhoods to the lake and to each other.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Chestermere's retail infrastructure has expanded significantly to serve its growing population. Chestermere Station Shopping Centre is the city's main commercial hub, anchored by Safeway and Shoppers Drug Mart and complemented by Dollarama, Browns Socialhouse, Tim Hortons, and a variety of local services. Just minutes away, the massive East Hills Shopping Centre on the Calgary side of the city boundary offers big-box retail including Costco, Walmart, Marshalls, PetSmart, and a Cineplex theatre — making it a one-stop destination for weekly errands and entertainment. A growing number of local restaurants, cafés, and boutique businesses have also emerged along the Chestermere Boulevard corridor as the city's commercial base matures.

Real Estate in Chestermere

The Chestermere real estate market in 2026 is active and appreciating, though it remains more affordable than many comparable Calgary communities on a per-square-foot basis. The average sold price across all home types sits around $717,000 — up approximately 11% from August 2025 — while the average listing price is approximately $790,000. Entry-level detached homes are available from around $480,000, representing 20–30% savings compared to similar-sized homes in Calgary's core. Townhomes average around $508,000, making them an attractive entry point for first-time buyers. Current inventory sits at approximately 333 active listings, including 223 detached homes, 98 townhomes, and 11 condos, giving buyers meaningful choice without the frenzied competition seen in some Calgary communities.

Several new communities are actively developing in Chestermere, including master-planned neighbourhoods with a mix of single-family homes, semi-detached, townhomes, and multi-family options. Location & Getting Around

Community Feel & Lifestyle
